svg.aria-label: From about 100 sampled poses to a selectivity decision: poses are grouped into binding modes, the best pose of each mode is scored against the target and a look-alike protein, and a bootstrap turns the difference into a delta-delta-G with a 95 percent interval. Illustration, not measured data.
svg.text: From about 100 poses to a selectivity decision
Illustration with made-up scores. The steps, the ΔΔG definition and the bootstrap are the real ones.
★ = the best-ranked pose of each binding mode
Score each mode against two proteins
top-ranked modes of each protein are averaged
ΔΔG (kcal/mol), 4,000 bootstrap resamples of the binding modes
The 95% interval stays below zero: the peptide prefers the target
The target is bound about 8 times more tightly (a factor of 8 in Kd).
The model's systematic bias affects both proteins the same way and cancels in the difference, which is why we compare against the same receptor and trust ΔΔG more than a single absolute ΔG.
